FOREWORD 


This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Pesticides 
Sectional Committee had been approved by the Food and Agriculture Divisional Council. 


Fipronil + Acetamiprid suspension concentrate (SC) is used as insecticide in agriculture. Fipronil + Acetamiprid 
SC formulation is generally manufactured to contain a mixture of 4.0 percent (m/m) of fipronil and 4.0 percent 
(m/m) of acetamiprid. 


In the preparation of this standard, due consideration has been given to the provisions of Insecticides Act, 1968 
and the rules framed thereunder. However, this standard is subject to the restrictions imposed under the 
Insecticides Act and rules, wherever applicable. 


The composition of the Committee responsible for the formulation of this standard is given in Annex H. 


For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, 
observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with 
IS 2 : 2022 ‘Rules for rounding off numerical values (second revision)’. The number of significant places retained 
in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 


IS 18390 : 2023 


Indian Standard 


FIPRONIL + ACETAMIPRID SUSPENSION 
CONCENTRATE — SPECIFICATION 


1 SCOPE 


This standard prescribes the requirements and the 
methods of sampling and test for Fipronil + 
Acetamiprid suspension concentrate. 


2 REFERENCES 


The standards listed in Annex A contain provisions 
which through reference in this text, constitute 
provisions of this standard. At the time of 
publication, the editions indicated were valid. All 
standards are subject to revision, and parties to 
agreements based on this standard are encouraged 
to investigate the possibility of applying the most 
recent edition of these standards. 


3 REQUIREMENTS 

3.1 Constituents 

3.1.1 The material shall consist of a suspension of 
fine particles of fipronil and acetamiprid, technical, 


in ап aqueous phase together with suitable 
formulants. 


3.1.2 Fipronil, technical conforming to IS 18389 and 
acetamiprid, technical conforming to IS 15981 shall 
be employed in the formulation of the material. 

3.2 Physical 

3.2.1 Description 


The material shall be of off white to cream 
homogenous liquid free from any visible impurities. 


3.2.2 Pourability 

When determined by the method prescribed in 
Annex С, the rinsed residue shall not be more than 1 
percent (m/m). 

3.2.3 Spontaneity of Dispersion 

When determined by the method prescribed in 


Annex D, the spontaneity of dispersion of the 
material shall not be less than 70 percent (m/m). 


3.2.4 Suspensibility 


When determined by the method prescribed in 
Annex E, the suspensibility of the material shall not 
be less than 75 percent (m/m). 


3.2.5 Persistent Foam 


When determined by the method prescribed in 
Annex F, the persistent foam shall not be more than 
60 ml in 12 min. 


3.2.6 Wet Sieve Test 


Not less than 98 percent by mass of the material shall 
pass through a 45 micron IS sieve when determined 
by method described in Annex G. 


3.3 Chemical 


The material shall comply with the chemical 
requirements specified in 3.3.1 and 3.3.2. 


3.3.1 Fipronil and Acetamiprid Content 


When determined by the method prescribed in 
Annex B, the observed fipronil and acetamiprid 
content, percent (m/m) of any of the samples shall 
not differ from the declared nominal value by more 
than tolerance limits indicated below: 


Nominal Value, Tolerance, 
percent percent 
Up to 9 +10 
-5 
Above 9 and +5 of the 
below 50 nominal 
value 
50 and above +5 
-3 


The actual value of fipronil and acetamiprid content 
in the formulation shall be calculated to the second 
decimal place and then rounded off to first decimal 
place before applying the tolerance given in 3.3.1 


IS 18390 : 2023 


3.3.2 Acidity/Alkalinity 


When tested by the method prescribed in IS 6940, 
the acidity (as H2SOx) or alkalinity (as NaOH) of the 
material shall not be more than 0.5 percent by mass, 
respectively. 


4 PACKING 


The material shall be packed in high density 
polyethylene (HDPE)  containers/bottles оғ 
capacities 100 ml, 250 ml, 500 ml and 1 litre. The 
HDPE containers for packing of material shall 
conform to IS 9754. These shall be further packed in 
5 ply corrugated boxes of 10 x 1 litre, 
20 ml x 500 ml, 40 ml x 250 ml. The corrugated 
boxes for packing of the material shall conform to 
IS 2771 (Part 1). The containers shall also conform 
to the various general requirements stipulated in 
IS 8190 (Part 2). 


5 MARKING 


The containers shall be securely closed and the 
following information shall be marked legibly and 
indelibly on each container: 


a) Name of the material; 

b) Name and address of the manufacturer; 

c) Batch number; 

d) Date of manufacture; 

e) Date of expiry; 

f) Net quantity; 

g) Nominal fipronil content, percent (m/m); 

h) Nominal acetamiprid content, percent 
(m/m); 


j) A cautionary notice as worded in the 
Insecticide Act, 1968, and rules framed 
thereunder; and 

k) Any other information required under the 
Legal Metrology (Packaged Commodities) 
Rules, 2011. 


5.2 BIS Certification Marking 


The product(s) conforming to the requirements of 
this standard may be certified as per the conformity 
assessment schemes under the provisions of the 
Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 and the Rules 
and Regulations framed thereunder, and the 
products may be marked with the Standard Mark. 


6 SAMPLING 


Representative samples of the material shall be 
drawn according to IS 10627. 


7 TESTS 


Tests shall be carried out by the appropriate methods 
referred in clauses 3.2.2 to 3.2.6, 3.3.1 and 3.3.2. 


7.2 Quality of Reagents 


Unless specified otherwise, pure chemicals and 
reagent grade water (see IS 1070) shall be employed 
in tests. 


NOTE — ‘Pure chemicals’ shall mean chemicals that do not 
contain impurities, which affect the results of analysis.

ANNEX B 
(Clause 3.3.1) 
DETERMINATION OF ACTIVE INGREDIENTS IN FIPRONIL + ACETAMIPRID SC 


B-1 GENERAL 


Two methods (Method I and Method II) have been 
specified for determination of active ingredients in 
Fipronil + Acetamiprid SC. Both the methods use 
high performance liquid chromatography technique. 
In Method I, the active ingredients іп the 
formulation are determined in separate run while in 
Method П, both the ingredients in the formulation 
are determined in a single run. Method II shall be 
referee method in case of any dispute. 


B-2 METHOD I 


B-2.1 Determination of Fipronil Content in 
Fipronil + Acetamiprid SC 


B-2.1.1 Apparatus 


B-2.1.1.1 High performance liquid chromatography 
equipped with a constant flow pump, sample 
injector capable of injecting 20 ul aliquots and an 
ultraviolet detector coupled to chromatography 
software and printer is used for this determination: 


Instrument HPLC with UV detector and 
suitable chromatography soft- 
-ware 

Column Silica, 25 cm x 4.6 mmi.d., 5 um 
particle size 

Mobile 2 percent isopropyl alcohol in 

Phase cyclohexane 

Flow Rate 1.2 ml/min. 

Injection 20 wl 

Volume 

Detector Ultraviolet detector (280 nm) 


B-2.1.1.2 Analytical balance 

B-2.1.1.3 Microlitre syringe — 25 Ш capacity 
B-2.1.1.4 Ultrasonic bath 

B-2.1.1.5 Standard glassware 

B-2.1.2 Reagents 

B-2.1.2.1 Isopropyl alcohol — HPLC grade 


В-2.1.2.2 Cyclohexane — HPLC grade 


B-2.1.2.3 Fipronil reference standard — of known 
purity 


B-2.1.3 Procedure 


B-2.1.3.1 Preparation of the standard solution 


Weigh about 0.1 g of fipronil standard in 50 ml of 
volumetric flask. Add isopropyl alcohol and dilute 
upto the mark. Then pipette out 10 ml of above 
solution, transfer it in a 50 ml of volumetric flask 
and dilute with cyclohexane upto the mark. 


B-2.1.3.2 Preparation of sample solution 


Weigh about a quantity of sample equivalent to 
0.1 g of fipronil in 50 ml of volumetric flask. Add 
isopropyl alcohol and dilute upto the mark. Then 
pipette out 10 ml of above solution, transfer it in a 
50 ml of volumetric flask and dilute with 
cyclohexane upto the mark. 


B-2.1.3.3 Inject the standard solution (В-2.1.3.1) 
and the sample solution (B-2.1.3.2) in replicate till 
consistent readings are obtained and calculate the 
fipronil content as given in B-2.1.4. 


B-2.1.4 Calculation 


Fipronil content, percent by mass = 


ADM „p 
М. x Ay 
where 
Аз = peak area of fipronil in sample 
solution; 
Mı = Mass, in ©, of standard fipronil; 
Р = percentage purity of standard; 
Mz = mass, іп ©, of sample taken for 
test; and 
Ау = peak area of fipronil in standard 
solution. 


B-2.2 Determination of Acetamiprid Content in 
Fipronil + Acetamiprid SC 


B-2.2.1 Apparatus 


B-2.2.1.1 High performance liquid chromatograph 
equipped with a constant flow pump, sample 
injector capable of injecting 20 ul aliquots and ап 
ultraviolet detector coupled to chromatography 


software and printer is used for this determination: 


Instrument HPLC with UV detector and 
suitable chromatography 
software 

Column ODS C 18, (25 cm x 3.9 mm 
i.d., 5 u) 

Mobile Acetonitrile : Water 

Phase Phosphoric acid (85 percent) 
(30 : 70 : 0.35 v/v) 

Flow Rate 1.0 ml/min 

Injection 20 ul 

Volume 

Detector Ultraviolet detector (280 nm) 


B-2.2.1.2 Analytical balance 

B-2.2.1.3 Microlitre syringe — 25 ul capacity 
B-2.2.1.4 Ultrasonic bath 

B-2.2.1.5 Standard glassware 

B-2.2.2 Reagents 


B-2.2.2.1 Phosphoric acid — AR grade 
B-2.2.2.2 Acetonitrile — HPLC grade 
B-2.2.2.3 Water — HPLC grade 


B-2.2.2.4 Acetamiprid reference standard — of 
known purity 


B-2.2.3 Procedure 


B-2.2.3.1 Preparation of the standard solution 


Weigh about 0.08 g of acetamiprid reference 
standard and dilute to 50 ml with acetonitrile. Dilute 
5 ml of this solution to 100 ml with mobile phase. 


B-2.2.3.2 Preparation of sample solution 


Weigh an amount of sample equivalent to 0.08 g of 
acetamiprid and dilute to 50 ml with acetonitrile. 
Dilute 5 ml of this solution to 100 ml with mobile 
phase. 


B-2.2.3.3 Inject the standard solution (B-2.2.3.1) 
and sample solution (B-2.2.3.2) in replicate till 
consistent readings are obtained and calculate the 
acetamiprid content as given in В-2.2.4. 


B-2.2.4 Calculation 
Acetamiprid content, percent by mass =

B-3 METHOD II 


B-3.1 Determination of Fipronil and Acetamiprid 
Contents in Fipronil + Acetamiprid SC 


B-3.1.1 Apparatus 


B-3.1.1.1 High performance liquid chromatograph 
equipped with a constant flow pump, sample 
injector capable of injecting 20 ul aliquots and an 
ultraviolet detector coupled to chromatography 
software and printer is used for this determination: 


Instrument HPLC with UV detector and 
suitable chromatography soft- 
-ware 

Column Nucleosil C18 (5 um); 250 mm 


x 4.6 mm i.d., or equivalent. 
Mobile Phase Acetonitrile + Water (70 + 30) 


Flow Rate 1.0 ml/min 

Injection 20 ul 

Volume

Temperature Ambient 


Retention Fipronil — 8.0 min approx. 
time Acetamiprid — 3.0 min approx. 


B-3.1.1.2 Analytical balance 

B-3.1.1.3 Microlitre syringe — 25 ul capacity 
B-3.1.1.4 Ultrasonic bath 

B-3.1.1.5 Standard glassware 

B-3.1.2 Reagents 

B-3.1.2.1 Standard reference — of known purity 
B-3.1.2.2 Acetonitrile — HPLC grade 


B-3.1.2.3 Water — HPLC grade 


IS 18390 : 2023 


B-3.1.3 Procedure 
B-3.1.3.1 Preparation of standard solution 


Weigh about 0.05 g of fipronil standard and 0.05 g 
of acetamiprid standard into volumetric flask 
(50 ml) and add 25 ml acetonitrile into flask and 
place the flask in ап ultrasonic bath for 
approximately 5 min. Allow it to attain room 
temperature and make up the volume up to the mark 
with acetonitrile and mix thoroughly. 


Pipette out 5.0 ml of solution into a 25 ml volumetric 
flask and makeup to the mark with acetonitrile and 
homogenize. 


B-3.1.3.2 Preparation of sample solution 


Weigh a quantity of sample so as to contain 0.05 g 
of fipronil and 0.05 g of acetamiprid standard into 
50 ml volumetric flask and add 25 ml of acetonitrile 
into flask and place the flask in an ultrasonic bath 
for approximately 5 min. Allow it to attain room 
temperature and make up the volume up to the mark 
with acetonitrile and mix thoroughly. 


Pipette out 5.0 ml of solution into a 25 ml volumetric 


flask and makeup to the mark with acetonitrile and 
homogenize. 


B-3.1.3.3 Inject 20 ul of the calibration solution C1 
until the consecutive relative response factors agree 
within 1 percent. Then, inject the standard and 
sample solutions in sequent. 


B-3.1.4 Calculation 


Fipronil/acetamiprid content, percent by mass = 


М, 1 Х Аз x P 
Мх A 
where 

Мү = mass, in g, of fipronil/acetamiprid 
standard; 

Аз = area of fipronil/acetamiprid peak in 
the sample; 

Р = percentage purity of 
fipronil/acetamiprid standard; 

Mı = mass, in g, of fipronil/acetamiprid 
sample; and 

A; = area of fipronil/acetamiprid peak 


in the standard.

ANNEX C 
(Clause 3.2.2) 
DETERMINATION OF POURABILITY IN FIPRONIL + ACETAMIPRID SC 


C-1 OUTLINE OF THE METHOD 


The suspension concentrate is allowed to stand for a 
definite time and the amount remaining in the 
container after a standardized pouring procedure is 
determined. The container is rinsed and the amount 
then remaining is determined. 


C-1.1 Apparatus/Equipment 


C-1.1.1 A 500 ml stoppered measuring cylinder as 
per following requirements: 


a) Volume equivalent to : 5ml 
1 subdivision of the 
scale 


b) Capacity corresponding : 50ml 
to lowest graduation 
mark 


c) Capacity corresponding : 500ml 
to highest graduation 


mark 
d) Length of scale : 250mm 
e) Overall height : 39cm 
f) Diameter of base : 10cm 
g) Stopper : B34 


NOTE — High density polyethylene bottles, 1 000 ml 
volume and Kilner jars, 700 ml volume, can be used but this 
must be recorded with the result. 


C-1.2 Procedure 


Weigh the empty container and stopper (Wo) and 
add enough of the test item taken from a recently 
mixed bulk sample to leave approximately 20 
percent of the volume of the container as ullage. 
Replace the stopper and reweigh the container 
(W,). Allow the container to stand undisturbed for 


24 h and then pour out the test item (see Note 1) for 
60 s at an angle of 45° and then finally invert the 
container for 60 s (see Note 2). Re-weigh the 
container and stopper (W2). Add distilled water at 
20 °C (a volume of 80 percent of that of the 
container) and replace the stopper. Invert the 
container 10 times (see Note 3) and empty the 
container as before and re-weigh the container and 
stopper (W3). Calculate the residue (R) and the 
rinsed residue (В). 


C-1.3 Calculation 


Е И’, – №; 
Residue (В), percent by mass = 20° x 100 
И = Wo 
Rinsed residue (К), percent by mass = 
Из = И, 
0 100 
И = Wo 
where 
W2 = mass, ing, of the container after the 
pouring out of the suspension 
concentrate; 
Wo = mass, in 5, of the empty container; 
У = mass, ing, of the container with the 
sample; and 
W3 = mass, in g, of the container after 
removal of distilled water. 
NOTES 


1 The length of the standing period and the temperature 
should be agreed previously. 


2 A square sided container should be held so that a flat side 
is underneath. 


3 The term invert the container means that the container’s 
vertical axis is turned through 180 °C and then brought back 
to its original position, the whole operation taking about 
2s.

ANNEX D 
(Clause 3.2.3) 
DETERMINATION OF SPONTANEITY OF DISPERSION IN FIPRONIL + ACETAMIPRID SC 


D-1 OUTLINE OF THE METHOD 


The method is broadly similar to that used to 
determine the suspensibility of concentrates, except 
that it employs only one inversion and a 5 min 
standing time. It involves preparing 250 ml of a 
mixture of formulation and water, mixed only with 
one inversion of the cylinder. After standing under 
defined conditions the top nine-tenths is removed, 
and the remaining tenth assayed chemically or by 
solvent extraction. The spontaneity of dispersion is 
readily calculated. 


D-2 REAGENT 
Standard hard water 
D-3 APPARATUS 


Graduated cylinders, glass stoppered, 250 ml 
capacity. Glass suction tubes about 40 cm long, 5 
mm internal diameter (i.d.) drawn out at one end to 
2 mm to 3 mm internal diameter (i.d). 


D-4 PROCEDURE 


Normally the whole procedure is carried out in 
duplicate. Homogenize the sample by gently 
stirring. The standard hard water, measuring 
cylinder and sample to be used in the determination 
should be equilibrated to the required temperature 
before starting the test. Determine the density of the 
formulation and calculate the mass of formulation 
equivalent to 12.5 ml (W g). Pour standard water 
(237.5 ml) at the required temperature into the 
graduated cylinder and stand this on a top-pan 
balance, tare the weight add the calculated mass of 
formulation from a small beaker held so that the lip 
is | cm above the top of the cylinder. Complete the 
addition within a time limit of 15 s. Record the 


weight of the formulation added. As soon as the 
formulation has been added, stopper the cylinder 
and invert once. Stand the cylinder in an upright 
position on a bench free from vibration or direct 
sources of heat for 5 min + 10 $. At the end of this 
time, carefully remove the stopper and withdraw 
the top 225 ml of suspension by means of the 
suction tube connected to a reservoir and suitable 
pump. Carry out the operation in 10 s to 15 s by 
maintaining the tip of the tube just below the falling 
level of the suspension, care being taken to 
minimize any disturbance of the suspension. Ensure 
that the tip of the tube is always only a few mm 
below the surface of the suspension. 


Transfer the 25 ml of dilute suspension remaining in 
the cylinder. Extract the active ingredient just like in 
suspensibility and calculate the spontaneity of 
dispersion. Determine the active ingredient content 
in the 25 ml bottom suspension. 


D-5 CALCULATION 


Spontaneity of dispersion, percent by mass = 


111 (C-Q) 
С 
where 
С =_ИЙХа = mass, іп g, in the whole 
100 cylinder; 

Q = mass, іп ©, of active ingredient 
in 25 ml sample at the bottom; 

W = mass, іп g, of formulation actually 
added to the cylinder; and 

a = percentage of active ingredient by 


mass in formulation.

ANNEX E 
(Clause 3.2.4) 
DETERMINATION OF SUSPENSIBILITY IN FIPRONIL + ACETAMIPRID SC 


E-1 REAGENTS 

Standard hard water 

E-2 APPARATUS 

Beaker and glass rod 

E-3 PROCEDURE (FOR FIPRONIL) 


Carry out the whole procedure in duplicate. 
Homogenize the sample Бу gently stirring 
(see Note 1). The mass of sample to be taken is that 
required to make 250 ml of diluted suspension, with 
the concentration recommended on the label. If a 
range of concentrations is recommended, the highest 
and lowest should be used (see Note 2). The 
standard hard water, measuring cylinder and sample 
to be used in the determination should be 
equilibrated to the required temperature. 


Place 100 ml of equilibrated standard water in a 
250 ml measuring cylinder. Weigh the required 
amount of sample into a 50 ml beaker and transfer 
quantitatively to the cylinder with more standard 
water, finally making up to 250 ml. Stopper the 
cylinder and invert 30 times (see Note 3). Place the 
cylinder in an upright position, free from vibration, 
and allow it to stand undisturbed for 30 min. 


At the end of the time, quickly insert the glass tube 
into the cylinder and by means of a vacuum pump 
and suitable reservoir withdraw nine-tenths (225 ml) 
of the suspension. Carry out the operation in 10 s to 
15 $ by maintaining the tip of the glass tube just 
below the falling level of the suspension, care being 
taken to minimize any disturbance of the suspension 
(see Note 4). 


Transfer the (25 + 1) ml of dilute suspension 
remaining in the cylinder to an evaporation dish and 
evaporate the water to dryness over a water bath. 
Record the weight of the residue. Find out the 
quantity (Q) of active ingredient in the residue by 
multiplying weight of residue with the assayed 
percent active ingredient content in the formulation 
(see Annex B) and dividing by 100. Calculate the 
suspensibility as given in E-4. 


NOTES 


1 A crust of dry material sometimes forms inside the neck 
of suspension concentrate containers. Care must be taken to 
ensure that particles do not break away from this and 
contaminate the sample used for the determination. 


2 It may be helpful to weigh the beaker plus formulation 
before and after the addition to the water to make a check 
on the amount of sample added to the water. 


3 To invert the cylinder, hold it with one hand at each 
end, insulated with a cloth, and rotate it through 180 °C 
and back again, through an imaginary fixed point 
midway between the hands. Ensure no bouncing occurs. 
Each inversion should take 2 s. 


4 It may be helpful to fit a rubber bung, larger than the 
cylinder mouth, as an adjustable stop so that the final 
level of suspension left in the cylinder is repeatable. The 
position of the bung can be determined by a preliminary 
calibration.

Carry out the whole procedure in duplicate. 
Homogenize the sample Бу gently stirring 
(see Note 1). The mass of sample to be taken is that 
required to make 250 ml of diluted suspension, with 
the concentration recommended on the label. If a 
range of concentrations is recommended, the highest 
and lowest should be used (see Note 2). The 
standard hard water, measuring cylinder and sample 
to be used in the determination should be 
equilibrated to the required temperature. 


Place 100 ml of equilibrated standard water in a 
250 ml measuring cylinder. Weigh the required 
amount of sample into a 50 ml beaker and transfer 
quantitatively to the cylinder with more standard 
water, finally making up to 250 ml. Stopper the 
cylinder and invert 30 times (see Note 3). Place the 
cylinder in an upright position, free from vibration, 
and allow it to stand undisturbed for 30 min. 


At the end of the time, quickly insert the glass tube 
into the cylinder and by means of a vacuum pump 
and suitable reservoir withdraw nine-tenths (225 ml)

of the suspension. Carry out the operation in 10 s to 
15 $ by maintaining the tip of the glass tube just 
below the falling level of the suspension, care being 
taken to minimize any disturbance of the suspension 
(see Note 4). 


Transfer the (25 + 1) ml of dilute suspension 
remaining in the cylinder to an evaporation dish and 
evaporate the water to dryness over a water bath. 
Record the weight of the residue. Find out the 
quantity (Q) of active ingredient in the residue by 
multiplying weight of residue with the assayed 
percent active ingredient content in the formulation 
(see Annex B) and dividing by 100. Calculate the 
suspensibility as given in E-6. 


NOTES 


1 A crust of dry material sometimes forms inside the neck 
of suspension concentrate containers. Care must be taken to 
ensure that particles do not break away from this and 
contaminate the sample used for the determination. 


2 It may be helpful to weigh the beaker plus formulation 
before and after the addition to the water to make a check 
on the amount of sample added to the water. 


10 


3 To invert the cylinder, hold it with one hand at each end, 
insulated with a cloth, and rotate it through 180°C and back 
again, through an imaginary fixed point midway between 
the hands. Ensure no bouncing occurs. Each inversion 
should take 2 s. 


4 It may be helpful to fit a rubber bung, larger than the 
cylinder mouth, as an adjustable stop so that the final level 
of suspension left in the cylinder is repeatable. The position 
of the bung can be determined by a preliminary calibration. 


E-6 CALCULATION (FOR ACETAMIPRID) 


ам 111 (c- 0) 
Suspensibility, percent by mass = =a 
where 

axw : : : 
= — po = Mass, in g, in the whole cylinder; 
О = mass, in, © of active ingredient in 
25 ml sample at the bottom; 
а = percent by mass of active ingredient 
in the formulation; and 
W = mass, in ©, of formulation actually 


added to the cylinder.

ANNEX F 
(Clause 3.2.5) 
DETERMINATION OF PERSISTANT FOAM IN FIPRONIL + ACETAMIPRID SC 


F-1 OUTLINE OF THE METHOD 


The suspension concentrate is diluted in a measuring 
cylinder of standard dimensions which is inverted 
30 times and, the amount of foam created and 
remaining after certain time is measured. 


F-2 APPARATUS 

F-2.1 Graduated Cylinder 

Glass stoppered of 250 ml capacity, with 2 ml 
graduations. The distance between the 0 mark and 
the 250 ml mark should be 20 cm to 21.5 cm and 
between the 250 ml mark and the bottom of the 
stoppered, 6 cm to 8 cm (the cylinder should be 
clean and free from grease). 

F-2.2 Stopwatch 

F-3 REAGENT 

Standard water 


F-4 PROCEDURE 


The mass of sample to be taken is that mass required 


to make 200 ml of a diluted formulation with a 
concentration recommended in the directions for use 
supplied with the product. When several 
concentrations are recommended, the maximum 
concentration shall be used. 


Put about 180 ml of standard hard water into the 
250 ml measuring cylinder standing on a top pan 
balance and weigh in the required amount of the 
sample. Fill to 200 ml with standard hard water and 
record the temperature (see Note 1). Stopper the 
cylinder and then invert it 30 times by hand through 
180 degrees and back to its original position, the 
whole operation being completed in approximately 
2 $. Place the stoppered cylinder upright on the bench 
and immediately start the stopwatch. Read the 
volume of foam produced and remaining after 12 min 
(see Note 2). 


NOTES 
1 The recommended temperature is 25 °C +5 °C. 


2 A few bubbles round the periphery are not significant. 
Any volumes above the 250 ml mark should be marked on 
the outside and the volume of foam thus determined. 


IS 18390 : 2023 


ANNEX G 
(Clause 3.2.6) 
DETERMINATION OF WET SIEVE TEST IN FIPRONIL + ACETAMIPRID SC 


G-1 PRINCIPLE 


The method is suitable for the determination of the 
amount of the non-dispersible material in Fipronil + 
Acetamiprid SC. 


G-2 APPARATUS 


G-2.1 Test Sieve — specified IS Sieve 
[see IS 460 (Part 1)] prepared for the test by 
removing any film, grease or any other water 
repellant material and then by drying. 


G-2.2 Rubber Hose — of 10 mm internal 
diameter. 


G-3 PROCEDURE 

G-3.1 Wet Sieving 

Transfer 10 g of the sample to the sieve, rinsing with 
tap water. Wash the material on the sieve with an 


oscillating jet of tap water. Using a rubber hose of 
10 mm i.d. delivering 4 litres to 5 litres of water per 


min. Continue the washing for 10 min, directing the 
water from the circumference of the sieve towards 
the center and keeping the end of the hose at a 
distance of between 2 cm to 5 cm from the surface 
of sieve. Transfer the residue to a pre weighed watch 
glass with a jet of distilled water from a wash bottle. 
Dry to constant weight and record the weight of the 
sample to the nearest 0.01 g. 


G-4 CALCULATION 


Material passing through the IS sieve, percent by 
mass = 


т 
100 (1 - т. 


where 


m = mass, in g, of the dry residue obtained; 
and 
M = mass, in g, of the material taken for test. 


IS 18390 : 2023

Bureau of Indian Standards 


BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 to promote harmonious 
development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods and attending to 
connected matters in the country. 


Copyright 


BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in any form without 
the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in the course of implementing the 
standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or grade designations. Enquiries relating to 
copyright be addressed to the Head (Publication & Sales), BIS. 


Review of Indian Standards 


Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed 
periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are 
needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards 
should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the website- 
www.bis.gov.in or www.standardsbis.in. 


This Indian Standard has been developed from Doc No.: FAD 01 (18799).
